prompt: Write the retry policy that database code needs: try again after a deadlock, give up instantly on broken SQL, and compute a capped doubling backoff. Complete runWithRetry and backoffMillis.
explanation: Retrying is only safe when the failure is transient -- a deadlock or lock timeout will probably succeed on a second attempt, while a syntax error never will, so the two exception types get different catch blocks. Ordering matters: the catch for the fatal type returns immediately, and the catch for the transient type simply falls through to the next turn of the loop. Exponential backoff with a cap keeps a struggling database from being hammered, while still bounding how long the caller waits.
hints: A for loop from 1 to maxAttempts with the database call inside a try is all the structure you need -- a successful call returns from inside the loop.
Write two catch blocks: catch (FatalDbException e) returns "FATAL", catch (TransientDbException e) does nothing so the loop tries again.
If the loop finishes without returning, every attempt failed transiently -- that is where the GAVE UP message belongs, and Math.max keeps a negative maxAttempts reporting 0.
